questions.question: A stone tied to a string is rotated in a circle. The force that acts towards the centre is—
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Centripetal force**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Centripetal force** is the force that acts towards the center of a circular path and is necessary for an object to move in a circular motion.
 
• When a **stone is tied to a string** and rotated in a circle, the tension in the string provides the centripetal force.
 
• The centripetal force is responsible for continuously changing the direction of the stone’s velocity, ensuring circular motion. *Hence, statement is correct.*
 
• Without centripetal force, the stone would move tangentially in a straight line due to inertia, as per **Newton's First Law of Motion**.
 
• The centripetal force does not cause the object to accelerate towards the center; it merely changes the direction of the velocity vector, maintaining circular motion.
 
• The magnitude of centripetal force can be calculated using the formula: **F = (mv²)/r**, where **m** is the mass of the object, **v** is the velocity, and **r** is the radius of the circle.
 
• *Hence, the correct answer is Centripetal force.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Centripetal Force:**

 
 
• **Centripetal force** is directed towards the center of the circular path and is essential for circular motion.
 
• Examples include: gravitational force keeping planets in orbit, tension in a string when rotating a stone, and frictional force enabling a car to turn on a curved road.
 
 
 
• **Centrifugal Force:**
 
 
• It is a **fictitious force** that appears to act outwardly on an object moving in a circle, experienced in a rotating reference frame.
 
• **Example:** When a car takes a sharp turn, passengers feel they are pushed outward, which is the effect of centrifugal force.
 
 
 
• **Other Forces (Incorrect Options):**
 
 
• **Frictional force:** Acts parallel to the surface and opposes motion. It is not responsible for circular motion in this case.
 
• **Gravitational force:** Acts between masses and is responsible for phenomena like planetary motion but not the circular motion of a stone tied to a string.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Newton’s Laws of Motion:**

 
 
• Circular motion requires a net inward force to continuously change the direction of motion. This is explained by **Newton's First Law**.
 
• The absence of centripetal force will result in the object moving tangentially due to inertia.
 
 
 
• **Applications of Centripetal Force:**
 
 
• Used in designing **roller coasters**, ensuring cars stay on curved paths in racing tracks, and satellites maintain their orbits.
 
• Important for understanding physical systems like planetary orbits, electron motion in circular accelerators, and spinning objects like centrifuges.

questions.question: Majority of the members of the Rajya Sabha are elected by:

options.text: the political parties that oppose the majority party
the elected members or ministers of different areas
the elected members of the legislative Assemblies of various states.

questions.solution:
Majority of the members of the Rajya Sabha are elected by __**the elected members of the legislative Assemblies of various states.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The Rajya Sabha is the upper house of the Indian Parliament, and it is **composed of 250 members. **
 
• Of these members, **238 are elected **by the elected members of the legislative assemblies of the various states. 
 
• The remaining** 12 members are nominated by the President of India.**
 
• The method of election for the Rajya Sabha is proportional representation by means of the single transferable vote. 
 
• This means that each voter has a number of votes equal to the number of seats that are being contested in their state. 
 
• They can cast their votes for as many candidates as they like, but they cannot give more than one vote to any one candidate.
 
• The votes are then counted, and the candidates who receive the most votes are elected. 
 
• If no candidate receives the majority of the votes, then the votes are transferred to the other candidates according to the preferences of the voters. 
 
• This process continues until all of the seats have been filled. 
 
• The **Rajya Sabha is a very important part **of the Indian Parliament. 
 
• It has the power to pass laws, approve the appointment of the Prime Minister, and impeach the President. 
 
• It also has the power to review laws passed by the Lok Sabha, the lower house of Parliament. 
 
• The Rajya Sabha is designed to represent the interests of the states in the Indian Parliament. 
 
• The fact that the majority of its members are elected by the elected members of the legislative assemblies of the various states ensures that the states have a strong voice in the national decision-making process.

questions.question: The average of 29 number is 38. The average of the first 19 numbers is 34 and that of the last 9 numbers is 48. The 20th number is.
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Average of 29 number is 38,

Average of the first 19 numbers is 34 and 

Average of the last 9 numbers is 48

**Formula used:**

Sum = Average × number 

**Calculation:**

Sum of all 29 numbers = Average × number = 38 × 29 = 1102

Sum of first 19 numbers = Average × number = 34 × 19 = 646

Sum of last 9 numbers = Average × number = 48 × 9 = 432

∴ 20th number = Sum of all 29 numbers - Sum of first 19 numbers - Sum of last 9 numbers

= 1102 - 646 - 432

= 24

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] **__Shortcut Trick__**

The average of 29 numbers is 38

The average of the first 19 numbers is 34, 

Which is (38 - 34) = 4 less than the total average,

So, the 19 numbers contribute 4 × 19 = 76 less 

Similarly, the average of the last 9 numbers is 48

Which is contributes (48 - 38) = 10 × 9 = 90 more

So, the net difference is (90 - 76) = 14

This extra 14 adjusted by 20th number, which is (38 - 14) = 24

questions.question: Why is DNA replication necessary?

options.text: For growth and formation of new cells

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**For growth and formation of new cells**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **DNA replication** is a crucial biological process where the DNA molecule copies itself to produce two identical strands. It ensures that genetic information is passed accurately from one cell generation to the next.
 
• Replication is necessary during **cell division** to ensure that each daughter cell receives an exact copy of the parent cell's DNA.
 
• The process supports **growth** and **development** in multicellular organisms by facilitating the formation of new cells. *Hence, the statement "For growth and formation of new cells" is correct.*
 
• DNA replication maintains the **integrity of genetic material** by reducing the chances of errors during cell division, ensuring proper functioning of living organisms.
 
• The replication process involves key enzymes like **DNA polymerase**, helicase, and ligase, which work together to unwind the DNA strand, replicate it, and seal the resulting fragments.
 
• It is essential in both **prokaryotic** and **eukaryotic organisms**, supporting their ability to reproduce, repair, and grow.
 
• *Hence, the correct answer is "For growth and formation of new cells."*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Importance of DNA replication:**

 
 
• **DNA replication** is essential for the **continuity of life**. It ensures that genetic material is passed from parent cells to daughter cells without loss of information.
 
• It plays a crucial role in supporting **growth, repair, and reproduction** of cells in both unicellular and multicellular organisms.
 
• Replication errors can lead to **mutations**, which may cause genetic disorders or contribute to evolution.
 
 
 
• **Mechanism of DNA replication:**
 
 
• DNA replication follows a **semi-conservative mechanism**, where each new DNA strand consists of one original strand and one newly synthesized strand.
 
• Important enzymes involved include:
 
 
• **Helicase:** Unwinds the double helix.
 
• **DNA polymerase:** Synthesizes new strands by adding complementary nucleotides.
 
• **Ligase:** Seals gaps between DNA fragments.
 
 
 
 
 
• **Applications:**
 
 
• DNA replication is utilized in **biotechnology** for techniques like **polymerase chain reaction (PCR)**, which amplifies DNA for research and diagnostics.
 
• It is also vital in **genetic engineering** and medical research to study genetic disorders and develop targeted therapies.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Incorrect options:**

 
 
• Option 1: "To stop cell division" is incorrect because DNA replication facilitates cell division rather than halting it.
 
• Option 3: "To reduce chromosome number" is incorrect as DNA replication doubles the DNA content rather than reducing it.
 
• Option 4: "To produce energy" is incorrect because DNA replication is not an energy-producing process; it consumes energy to synthesize new strands.
 
 
 
• **Biological Significance:**
 
 
• DNA replication ensures **genetic stability**, which is essential for maintaining the characteristics of species over generations.
 
• It contributes to **healing and repair** by allowing cells to divide and replace damaged or dead cells.

questions.question: Potential difference is—

options.text: Work done to move 1 C charge

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Work done to move 1 C charge**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Potential difference** is defined as the **work done per unit charge** to move a charge from one point to another within an electric field.
 
• It is expressed mathematically as **V = W/Q**, where:
 
 
• **V** is the potential difference (measured in volts).
 
• **W** is the work done (measured in joules).
 
• **Q** is the charge (measured in coulombs).
 
 
 
• Potential difference indicates the amount of energy required to move **1 coulomb (C)** of charge through an electric field. *Hence, this definition is correct.*
 
• **Statement Analysis:**
 
 
• **Option 1:** Heat per unit mass is incorrect because potential difference is unrelated to heat or mass.
 
• **Option 3:** Charge stored per unit area is incorrect because this relates to **capacitance**, not potential difference.
 
• **Option 4:** Energy of electrons is incorrect because potential difference refers to the work done on charges, not directly to electron energy.
 
 
 
• *Hence, option 2 is the correct answer.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Definition of Voltage:**

 
 
• **Voltage**, also known as electric potential difference, is a scalar quantity representing the difference in electric potential between two points in a circuit.
 
• It is measured in units of **volts** (V), where 1 volt = 1 joule/coulomb.
 
 
 
• **Applications of Voltage:**
 
 
• Voltage is used to drive electric currents in circuits, powering devices such as **lights, motors, and electronics.**
 
• It is also critical in fields like **electric power systems**, **battery technology**, and **semiconductor devices**.
 
 
 
• **Key Characteristics:**
 
 
• **Sources of Voltage:** Voltage can be generated through chemical reactions in batteries, electromagnetic induction in generators, or solar energy in photovoltaic cells.
 
• **Types of Voltage:** DC (Direct Current) voltage remains constant over time, while AC (Alternating Current) voltage varies periodically.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Misconceptions about Potential Difference:**

 
 
• Potential difference is often confused with **electric potential energy**. While related, potential difference refers specifically to energy per unit charge.
 
• It is also distinct from **electric current**, which measures the flow of charge, and **resistance**, which quantifies opposition to current.
 
 
 
• **Real-life Examples:**
 
 
• A **9V battery** provides 9 joules of energy for every coulomb of charge it moves.
 
• **Power outlets** in households typically supply 120V or 230V AC, depending on the country.
 
• **Electric cars** use high-voltage batteries (e.g., 400V) to power their motors efficiently.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a way to acquire citizenship in India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Renunciation**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Renunciation** is not a way to acquire citizenship in India; rather, it is a way to voluntarily give up Indian citizenship.
 
• The Citizenship Act, 1955, provides various modes for acquiring Indian citizenship, including **by birth, descent, registration, and naturalization**.
 
• **Incorporation of territory** is another mode where a new territory becomes a part of India, and the government may specify the persons who shall be citizens of India.
 
• Citizenship by **registration** is available to certain categories of persons such as persons of Indian origin who are ordinarily resident in India and other specified categories.
 
• Citizenship by **birth** is applicable to individuals born in India on or after January 26, 1950, but before July 1, 1987, and to individuals born on or after July 1, 1987, if either parent is a citizen of India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The Citizenship Act, 1955, also provides for the termination and deprivation of citizenship under specific conditions.
 
• Renunciation of citizenship is a voluntary act and can be done by any citizen of India who is also a citizen or national of another country.
 
• Upon renunciation, the individual ceases to be a citizen of India, and any minor child of that person also loses Indian citizenship.
 
• The process of renunciation is outlined in the Citizenship Rules, and it requires the individual to make a declaration in the prescribed manner.
 
• It's important for individuals to be aware of the implications of renunciation, including the loss of rights and privileges associated with Indian citizenship.

questions.question: A can do a piece of work in 12 days. He worked for 6 days and left, and then B finished it in 10 days. If both work together, then in how many days will they finish the same work?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

A can do a piece of work in 12 days

**Concept used:**

If a person can complete a work alone in x days, then the efficiency (part of the work completed in one day) = 1/x

**Calculation:**

A can do a piece of work in 12 days

So, In 1 day he does = 1/12 units

In 6 days he has done = 6/12 = 1/2 units

So, the remaining 1/2 is done by B in 10 days

So, B can do total work in 20 days

Now, 

In one day total work = 1/12 + 1/20

⇒ (5 + 3)/60

⇒ 8/60 = 2/15

So, they will take 15/2 days or 7.5 days

**∴ They will finish the same work in 7.5 days**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] **__Shortcut Trick__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4218c0b62c93a35c7c675a8495b1ce926211987acf52e6635eb742778978a3d2.png] 

Work done by A in 6 days = 30

Remaining work = 60 - 30 = 30

So the efficiency of B as he completes the work in 10 days = 30/10 = 3

Total time to complete the work by A and B is = 60 / 8 = 7.5 days

questions.question: What happens when a sound wave travels from air into water?

options.text: Frequency remains constant while wavelength changes
Wavelength stays constant but frequency rises

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Frequency remains constant while wavelength changes**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Sound Wave Characteristics:** When a sound wave moves from one medium (e.g., air) to another (e.g., water), its **speed and wavelength change**, but the **frequency remains constant**. This occurs because the frequency is determined by the source of the sound and does not depend on the medium.
 
• **Frequency:** The frequency of the sound wave remains constant during the transition because it is governed by the vibrating source. *Hence, the statement that frequency remains constant is correct.*
 
• **Wavelength:** The wavelength changes because it is influenced by the speed of sound in the new medium. Water has a higher density and elasticity than air, leading to a faster speed of sound and a longer wavelength in water. *Hence, the statement about wavelength change is correct.*
 
• **Speed of Sound:** The speed of sound increases as it enters water from air due to water’s greater density and elasticity compared to air. This change in speed directly impacts the wavelength, as wavelength is proportional to the speed of sound. *Hence, the statement about the speed increase is correct.*
 
• ***In summary:** When a sound wave travels from air to water, the **frequency remains constant** while the **wavelength increases** due to the higher speed of sound in water.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Speed of Sound in Different Media:**

 
 
• The speed of sound varies in different media due to their **density** and **elasticity**. It is approximately **343 m/s** in air, **1482 m/s** in water, and much faster in solids like steel (**5960 m/s**).
 
• The higher speed in water is due to its greater density and ability to transmit compressional waves more efficiently compared to air.
 
 
 
• **Relationship Between Speed, Frequency, and Wavelength:**
 
 
• The equation governing this relationship is **v = f × λ**, where:
 
 
• **v:** Speed of sound in the medium
 
• **f:** Frequency of the sound wave (constant)
 
• **λ:** Wavelength of the sound wave
 
 
 
• As the speed of sound increases in water, the wavelength increases proportionally, keeping the frequency constant.
 
 
 
• **Applications of Sound Waves in Different Media:**
 
 
• **Sonar Technology:** Utilizes the high speed of sound in water for underwater navigation and object detection.
 
• **Medical Imaging:** Ultrasound uses sound waves in water-based media to produce images of internal organs.
 
• **Acoustics:** Understanding sound propagation in air and water is essential for designing musical instruments and soundproof environments.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Physical Properties of Media:**

 
 
• **Density:** Water's higher density compared to air makes it a better medium for transmitting sound waves.
 
• **Elasticity:** The elasticity of the medium determines how efficiently sound waves propagate. Water’s higher elasticity contributes to the faster speed of sound.
 
 
 
• **Real-life Examples:**
 
 
• **Underwater Communication:** Submarines use sound waves to communicate and detect objects underwater.
 
• **Marine Exploration:** Scientists use sound waves to study ocean floors and marine life.

questions.question: The small intestine is divided into duodenum, jejunum and __________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Ileum**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **small intestine** is divided into three main parts: **duodenum, jejunum, and ileum**. These sections are vital for the digestion and absorption of nutrients.
 
• The **ileum** is the last and longest part of the small intestine. It connects the small intestine to the large intestine via the **ileocecal valve**.
 
• The ileum is specialized for the absorption of **vitamins, minerals, and nutrients**, especially **vitamin B12** and bile salts, which are crucial for maintaining metabolic processes.
 
• Unlike the jejunum and duodenum, the ileum has a higher density of **Peyer’s patches**, which are lymphoid tissues that play a role in immune function by monitoring intestinal bacteria.
 
• The ileum contains finger-like projections called **villi**, which enhance the surface area for nutrient absorption. These villi are covered by microvilli, further improving absorption efficiency.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Structure and Function of the Small Intestine:**

 
 
• The small intestine is approximately **6 meters long** and is divided into three parts: **duodenum, jejunum, and ileum.**
 
• The **duodenum** is the first section and is responsible for receiving partially digested food from the stomach and mixing it with bile and digestive enzymes.
 
• The **jejunum** is the middle section and is primarily involved in the absorption of sugars, amino acids, and fatty acids.
 
• The **ileum**, the final section, absorbs nutrients not absorbed by the jejunum, such as **vitamin B12 and bile salts**.
 
 
 
• **Large Intestine vs Small Intestine:**
 
 
• The **large intestine** is shorter (about 1.5 meters) and primarily absorbs water and salts while forming feces.
 
• The **small intestine** is longer and designed for nutrient absorption, with specialized structures like villi and microvilli.
 
• The small intestine connects to the large intestine via the **ileocecal valve**, ensuring the movement of digested food.
 
 
 
• **Digestive Functions of the Ileum:**
 
 
• The ileum absorbs **vitamins, fatty acids, and bile salts** essential for digestion.
 
• It contains specialized lymphoid tissues like **Peyer’s patches**, which help in immune surveillance.
 
• It is involved in recycling bile salts back to the liver, a process known as the **enterohepatic circulation**.
 
 
 
• **Key Features of the Small Intestine:**
 
 
• The small intestine has a large surface area due to the presence of **villi and microvilli**, facilitating efficient nutrient absorption.
 
• It is lined with enzymes that aid in breaking down carbohydrates, proteins, and fats into absorbable molecules.
 
• Its walls are rich in blood vessels, ensuring nutrients are transported into the bloodstream for distribution throughout the body.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Peyer’s patches:**

 
 
• These are specialized lymphoid tissues found in the ileum and play a critical role in the **immune system**.
 
• They monitor intestinal bacteria and prevent pathogenic bacteria from entering the bloodstream.
 
 
 
• **Ileocecal Valve:**
 
 
• This valve separates the ileum from the large intestine and prevents the backflow of contents into the small intestine.
 
• It ensures the proper movement of digested food for further processing in the large intestine.
 
 
 
• **Vitamin B12 Absorption:**
 
 
• The ileum absorbs **vitamin B12** bound to intrinsic factor, which is essential for **red blood cell formation** and neurological functions.

• **Hydrocarbons:** Organic compounds consisting of hydrogen and carbon atoms. Common fuels like natural gas and propane are hydrocarbons.

⇒ ∠C = 180° − 134° = 46°

⇒ Now, consider ▵AEC. Since point E lies on the line segment BC, extending side CE to point B forms the exterior angle ∠AEB at vertex E.

⇒ According to the exterior angle theorem, the measure of an exterior angle of a triangle is equal to the sum of the measures of its two remote interior opposite angles.

⇒ ∠AEB = ∠CAE + ∠C

⇒ ∠AEB = 23° + 46°

⇒ ∠AEB = 69°

**∴ The correct answer is 69°.**

Exterior Angle Theorem

The exterior angle of a triangle is exactly equal to the sum of the two opposite interior angles. Formula: ∠Exterior = ∠Int₁ + ∠Int₂.

Angle Sum Property

The sum of all interior angles of a triangle is always 180°. This fundamental property applies uniformly across all types of triangles in planar geometry.

In any right-angled triangle, the sum of the two acute angles is strictly 90°, as the right angle itself accounts for 90° out of the total 180° limit.

questions.question: Which of the following is a non-metal?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Sulphur**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Sulphur** is a **non-metal**, which is a chemical element with the atomic number **16**. It is classified as a non-metal because it does not possess metallic properties like luster, conductivity, or malleability.
 
• **Sulphur** is known for its bright yellow appearance and is solid at room temperature. It is brittle and cannot be shaped into sheets or wires, further confirming its non-metallic nature.
 
• Non-metals generally have low conductivity, and sulphur is a poor conductor of heat and electricity. This characteristic is a key differentiator between metals and non-metals. *Hence, Sulphur is the correct answer.*
 
• Other elements in the options like **Calcium**, **Magnesium**, and **Aluminium** are metals because they exhibit metallic properties such as good conductivity, malleability, and ductility. These elements cannot be classified as non-metals. *Hence, the other options are incorrect.*
 
• Non-metals like sulphur are essential in various chemical and biological processes. Sulphur is widely used in the production of fertilizers, matches, and insecticides. *This makes Sulphur significant among non-metals.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Characteristics of Non-Metals:**

 
 
• **Non-metals** are elements that lack metallic properties. They are usually brittle, dull, and poor conductors of heat and electricity.
 
• Examples of non-metals include **oxygen, nitrogen, carbon, sulphur, and chlorine**. These elements are essential for life and various industrial processes.
 
• Non-metals are commonly found in nature in gaseous, liquid, or solid forms. For instance, **sulphur** is solid, **oxygen** is gaseous, and **bromine** is liquid.
 
 
 
• **Uses of Sulphur:**
 
 
• **Sulphur** is used in the manufacturing of **fertilizers** like ammonium sulphate to enhance crop yield.
 
• It is a key component in the production of **matches, gunpowder, and insecticides** due to its chemical reactivity.
 
• Sulphur is also used in the vulcanization of rubber, a process that improves the durability and elasticity of rubber products.
 
 
 
• **Metallic Properties vs. Non-Metallic Properties:**
 
 
• **Metals** are malleable, ductile, lustrous, and good conductors of electricity and heat. Examples include **iron, copper, and aluminium**.
 
• In contrast, **non-metals** like sulphur are brittle, non-lustrous, and poor conductors.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **About the given options:**

 
 
• **Calcium:** A metal with atomic number **20**, known for its role in bone health and industrial applications.
 
• **Magnesium:** A metal with atomic number **12**, widely used in fireworks, medicines, and as an alloying agent.
 
• **Aluminium:** A metal with atomic number **13**, utilized in construction, transportation, and packaging industries due to its lightweight and corrosion resistance.
 
 
 
• **Physical and Chemical Properties:**
 
 
• Non-metals like sulphur typically form **acidic oxides**, whereas metals form basic oxides.
 
• **Sulphur** reacts with oxygen to produce **sulphur dioxide (SO₂)**, which is used in the food and beverage industry as a preservative.

questions.question: What type of combustion occurs when we bring a burning matchstick near a gas stove in the kitchen and turn on the knob of the gas stove?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Rapid combustion**__.

__
 
• **Rapid combustion** occurs when a substance burns quickly with the release of a large amount of heat and light.
 
• When a burning matchstick is brought near a gas stove, the LPG (Liquefied Petroleum Gas) ignites immediately, which is an example of rapid combustion.
 
• In this type of combustion, the fuel (LPG) mixes with oxygen from the air and burns swiftly.
 
• Rapid combustion is a controlled process in gas stoves, allowing us to use the released heat for cooking.
 
• Examples of rapid combustion include the burning of gasoline in engines, fireworks, and the ignition of a gas stove.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Combustion:** Combustion is a chemical process in which a substance reacts with oxygen to release energy in the form of heat and light.
 
• **Types of Combustion:** There are three types of combustion: rapid combustion, spontaneous combustion, and explosion.
 
• **Spontaneous Combustion:** This occurs without the application of external heat, such as the burning of phosphorus in air.
 
• **Slow Combustion:** This happens at a slow rate, releasing less heat and light, like the rusting of iron.
 
• **Safety Precautions:** While using LPG stoves, ensure proper ventilation and check for gas leaks to prevent accidental combustion or fire hazards.

questions.question: Power of lens is the reciprocal of its:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **power of a lens** is a measure of its ability to converge or diverge light rays.
 
• It is defined as the **reciprocal of the focal length** of the lens, expressed in meters.
 
• Mathematically, the formula for power is: **P = 1 / f**, where **P** is the power in diopters (D) and **f** is the focal length in meters.
 
• The unit of power is the **diopter (D)**, which represents a focal length of 1 meter.
 
• Lenses with **shorter focal lengths** have greater power and are more effective at bending light.
 
• For example, a lens with a focal length of 0.5 meters has a power of **2D (1/0.5 = 2)**.
 
• Positive power (e.g., +2D) indicates a **converging lens**, whereas negative power (e.g., -2D) indicates a **diverging lens**.
 
• This concept is widely used in applications such as **optometry** (to measure the refractive power of eyeglasses or contact lenses) and **optical instruments** like microscopes and telescopes.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Wavelength**__

 __
 
• **Wavelength** refers to the distance between two consecutive peaks or troughs in a wave.
 
• It is commonly associated with **light and sound waves**.
 
• Wavelength is measured in units like **meters, nanometers, or micrometers**, depending on the type of wave.
 
• In optics, wavelength is crucial for understanding phenomena like **diffraction, interference, and dispersion.**
 
 
 
• **Image Distance**__
 __
 
• **Image distance** refers to the distance between the lens and the image formed by it.
 
• It is denoted by the symbol **v** in lens formulas.
 
• It varies based on the type of lens (converging or diverging) and the position of the object.
 
• The lens formula is: **1/f = 1/v - 1/u**, where **u** is the object distance, **v** is the image distance, and **f** is the focal length.
 
 
 
• **Object Distance**__
 
 
• **Object distance** is the distance between the object and the lens or mirror.
 
• It is typically denoted by the symbol **u** in optical equations.
 
• The object distance plays a significant role in determining the image's position, size, and type (real or virtual).

questions.question: Which of the following best explains the functional diversity of RNA molecules in cells?

options.text: Their capability to act as adapter, structural and catalytic molecules
Their permanent role as genetic material
Their ability to form double-stranded helical structures

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Their capability to act as adapter, structural and catalytic molecules**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• RNA molecules exhibit functional diversity by acting as **adapter molecules** in translation, such as transfer RNA (tRNA), which brings amino acids to the ribosome.
 
• They serve as **structural components** in cellular machinery, such as ribosomal RNA (rRNA), which forms the core of ribosomes.
 
• RNA molecules can act as **catalysts**, such as ribozymes, which facilitate biochemical reactions without being proteins.
 
• RNA plays regulatory roles, such as microRNAs (miRNAs) and small interfering RNAs (siRNAs), which modulate gene expression post-transcriptionally.
 
• The versatility of RNA is due to its ability to adopt complex secondary and tertiary structures, enabling diverse functional roles in cellular processes.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Messenger RNA (mRNA):**

 
 
• Acts as a template for protein synthesis during translation.
 
• mRNA carries genetic information from DNA to ribosomes.
 
• Each mRNA sequence specifies the amino acid sequence of a protein.
 
 
 
• **Transfer RNA (tRNA):**
 
 
• tRNA functions as an adapter molecule in translation.
 
• It has anticodons that pair with mRNA codons and carries specific amino acids to the ribosome.
 
• tRNA’s cloverleaf structure is critical for its role in protein synthesis.
 
 
 
• **Ribosomal RNA (rRNA):**
 
 
• Forms the structural and functional core of ribosomes.
 
• rRNA helps in aligning mRNA and tRNA during translation.
 
• Some rRNA molecules exhibit catalytic activity, facilitating peptide bond formation.
 
 
 
• **Ribozymes:**
 
 
• RNA molecules with enzymatic properties.
 
• Examples include self-splicing introns and the RNA component of RNase P.
 
• Ribozymes demonstrate that RNA can act as both genetic material and a catalyst.

Let Original Income = 100%. Then Expenses = 100% − 18.5% = 81.5%.

Change in Savings = Increase in Income − Increase in Expenses = 17% − 32.6% = −15.6%

Percentage Change

• **Reflection of UV Rays by Glass:**

 
 
• Glass has a unique property of reflecting **ultraviolet (UV) rays** more efficiently compared to visible light.
 
• This phenomenon makes UV rays appear **brighter and more intense** when they strike a glass surface.
 
 
 
• **Absorption of UV Rays:**
 
 
• Ordinary glass typically absorbs a significant portion of UV rays, especially those with shorter wavelengths. However, the UV rays that are not absorbed are reflected, contributing to their apparent intensity. This is why the statement "glass completely absorbs UV rays" is incorrect.
 
 
 
• **Wavelength of UV Rays:**
 
 
• UV rays have **shorter wavelengths** than visible light. This shorter wavelength interacts differently with glass compared to longer wavelengths of visible light.
 
• The statement "the wavelength of UV rays is very long" is incorrect because UV rays are characterized by their short wavelengths.
 
 
 
• **Glass Producing Colored Light:**
 
 
• Glass does not inherently produce colored light when UV rays strike it. The interaction of UV rays with glass involves reflection and absorption, not the production of colors. Hence, the statement "glass produces colored light" is also incorrect.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Properties of Ultraviolet (UV) Rays:**

 
 
• UV rays are a type of electromagnetic radiation with wavelengths ranging from **10 nm to 400 nm**, shorter than visible light but longer than X-rays.
 
• They are categorized into three types: **UVA (315–400 nm)**, **UVB (280–315 nm)**, and **UVC (100–280 nm)**.
 
• UV rays are largely absorbed by the Earth's **ozone layer**, but some UVA and UVB rays reach the surface.
 
 
 
• **Interaction of UV Rays with Glass:**
 
 
• Ordinary glass blocks most UVB and UVC rays but allows a portion of UVA rays to pass through.
 
• Special types of glass, like **quartz glass**, can transmit more UV rays, while laminated or coated glass is designed to block UV rays effectively.
 
 
 
• **Applications of Glass in UV Protection:**
 
 
• Glass is often used in windows and eyewear to block harmful UV rays and protect individuals from exposure.
 
• Special coatings on glass can enhance its ability to reflect or absorb UV rays, making it suitable for use in **automobiles, buildings, and protective gear**.
 
 
 
• **Reflection Coefficient:**
 
 
• The reflection of UV rays by glass is determined by its **reflection coefficient**, which varies based on the angle of incidence and wavelength of the radiation.

questions.question: What is the relation between the speed of sound (v), its wavelength (λ) and time period (T)?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**v = λ / T**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Relation between speed, wavelength, and time period:** The speed of sound (**v**) in a medium is related to its wavelength (**λ**) and time period (**T**) by the formula: **v = λ / T**. This is a fundamental equation in wave mechanics.
 
• **Wavelength (λ):** This is the distance between two consecutive crests or troughs of a wave. It is measured in **meters (m)**.
 
• **Time Period (T):** This is the time taken for one complete oscillation or wave cycle. It is measured in **seconds (s)**.
 
• **Speed of sound (v):** This is the rate at which sound waves propagate through a medium. It is measured in **meters per second (m/s)**.
 
• The relationship can also be expressed in terms of **frequency** (f), as f = 1/T. Substituting f in the above formula gives v = λ × f.
 
• The formula highlights that the speed of sound is directly proportional to the wavelength and inversely proportional to the time period.
 
• *Hence, the correct answer is v = λ / T.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Wave Properties:**

 
 
• **Wavelength (λ):** It determines the spatial length of a wave and is inversely proportional to frequency for a constant speed of sound.
 
• **Time Period (T):** It is inversely related to frequency. A shorter time period corresponds to a higher frequency wave.
 
• **Frequency (f):** It is the number of oscillations per second, measured in **Hertz (Hz)**. Frequency is related to time period as f = 1/T.
 
 
 
• **Applications of Wave Mechanics:**
 
 
• **Acoustics:** Understanding the speed of sound is crucial in designing auditoriums and music halls.
 
• **Sonar Technology:** The relation between speed, wavelength, and time period is used in sonar systems for underwater exploration.
 
• **Communication:** Wave mechanics principles are applied in designing communication systems like radio and television.
 
 
 
• **Factors Affecting Speed of Sound:**
 
 
• The speed of sound depends on the **medium** through which it travels. It is faster in solids, slower in liquids, and slowest in gases.
 
• Temperature, pressure, and density of the medium also influence the speed of sound. For example, sound travels faster in warm air compared to cold air.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Alternative Representation:**

 
 
• The speed of sound can also be written as **v = λ × f**, where **f** is the frequency of the wave.
 
• This equation highlights the inverse relationship between wavelength and frequency when the speed is constant.
 
 
 
• **Practical Examples:**
 
 
• **Example:** In musical instruments, the pitch of a note is determined by the frequency of the sound wave, which is indirectly related to its time period.
 
• **Example:** In radar systems, the speed of electromagnetic waves is used to calculate distances using similar principles.

questions.question: Which type of reaction is involved in the rusting of iron?
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Redox**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Rusting of iron** is a chemical process where iron reacts with oxygen and moisture to form **iron oxides**, commonly called rust.
 
• This reaction involves both **oxidation** and **reduction**, hence it is categorized as a **redox reaction**.
 
• The **oxidation process** involves the loss of electrons by iron (Fe) as it forms ferrous (Fe²⁺) or ferric (Fe³⁺) ions.
 
• The **reduction process** involves oxygen being reduced by gaining electrons to form hydroxide ions (OH⁻) in the presence of water.
 
• The overall reaction can be written as:

 **4Fe + 3O₂ + 6H₂O → 4Fe(OH)₃**, which eventually dehydrates to form rust (Fe₂O₃·xH₂O).
 
• **Moisture and oxygen** are crucial for the rusting process, which is why it occurs more rapidly in humid environments.
 
• The formation of rust weakens the iron structure, causing damage to its strength and durability.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Displacement Reaction**__

 __
 
• A displacement reaction occurs when a more reactive element displaces a less reactive element from its compound. For example, **Zn + CuSO₄ → ZnSO₄ + Cu**.
 
• Rusting is not a displacement reaction as no exchange or replacement of elements occurs during the process.
 
 
 
• **Combination Reaction**__
 __
 
• In a combination reaction, two or more substances combine to form a single product. For example, **2H₂ + O₂ → 2H₂O**.
 
• Rusting is not a combination reaction because multiple reactions occur simultaneously, and it is not limited to just combining reactants into one product.
 
 
 
• **Decomposition Reaction**__
 
 
• A decomposition reaction involves the breakdown of a compound into two or more substances. For example, **CaCO₃ → CaO + CO₂**.
 
• Rusting is not a decomposition reaction, as it involves the formation of new compounds (iron oxides) rather than breaking down existing compounds.

questions.question: What is the dimensional formula of pressure?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**[ML⁻¹T⁻²]**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Pressure** is defined as the **force** applied per unit **area**.
 
• Mathematically, **Pressure = Force / Area**.
 
• **Force** has the dimensional formula **[MLT⁻²]**, where M = mass, L = length, T = time.
 
• **Area** has the dimensional formula **[L2]**.
 
• Dividing force by area gives **[MLT⁻²] / [L²] = [ML⁻¹T⁻²]**, which is the dimensional formula of pressure.
 
• **Applications:** Pressure is used in fields like **fluid mechanics, hydraulics, meteorology, and engineering design**.
 
• **Examples:** Atmospheric pressure, blood pressure, and pressure in hydraulic lifts.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **[ML⁻²T⁻²]**__: This dimensional formula corresponds to **surface tension**.

 __
 
• **Surface tension** represents force per unit **length** along the surface of a liquid.
 
• Common applications include **capillary action, formation of droplets, and liquid interfaces in engineering.**
 
 
 
• **[ML²T⁻²]**__: This represents **moment of force or torque**.
 __
 
• It is calculated as **Force × Distance** from the pivot.
 
• Used in applications such as **lever systems, mechanical rotation, and structural analysis.**
 
 
 
• **[MLT⁻²]**__: This is the dimensional formula for force itself.
 
 
• **Force** acts on objects to produce **acceleration**.
 
• Applications include **mechanics, dynamics, and structural design calculations.**
